title: Two ways to a store: wrap the web app you have, or write a native one

videos.script:
This course takes one small web app and puts it somewhere a browser tab cannot go. {{phone}} On a phone, as an Android and an iOS app. {{desktop}} On a desktop, as a program with its own window and its own installer.

There are two ways to do that, and they differ in who draws the screen. {{wrap}} In the first, your app runs as it is, inside a browser engine that a native app carries. {{native}} In the second, you describe the screens again, and the platform draws them with its own controls. Nothing converts one into the other. Knowing which a tool does tells you most of what it can do.

Today you meet the app. {{planner}} It is a study planner, five short files of TypeScript with no framework. You build it, you open it, and you read it the way a screen reader does. {{tree}}

And one thing is said now rather than later. {{mac}} Two lessons need a Mac. Everything else runs on the computer you have.
